title: BECE Business Studies: Office Practice - Business Studies - Office Correspondence
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Any written communication that passes between an organization and its customers, or among departments within the organization, is known as
questions.explain: **Office correspondence** refers to all forms of written communications (such as letters, memos, and emails) sent out or received by a business.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The first step taken by a clerk when a large batch of incoming physical mail is delivered to the office is to
questions.explain: Proper handling of mails begins with **sorting the mails**—separating official letters from private ones, and organizing them by department before opening them.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a standard way through which physical mails come into a business organization?
questions.explain: Mails commonly come in via the post office, courier agencies, and hand delivery by dispatch riders. **Telepathy** is a fictional mind-reading concept and not a communication medium.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A book used by the receptionist or mail clerk to record details of all letters leaving the organization is the
questions.explain: The **outgoing mail register** is specifically maintained to keep track of every letter or parcel dispatched from the office to external destinations.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Why is it a standard procedure to stamp official incoming mails with a date stamp immediately after opening them?
options: To make the letters look beautiful and professional
To hide the sender's address from junior staff
To officially show exactly when the letter was received by the office
To increase the physical weight of the letter for postage
questions.explain: Date-stamping is a critical mail handling procedure used **to officially show exactly when the letter was received**, providing evidence in case of delays or disputes.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which correspondence record is used to obtain a signature from a receiver as proof that a letter or parcel was physically delivered by hand?
questions.explain: A **Dispatch book** is carried by a messenger. When they deliver a letter by hand, the person receiving it signs the dispatch book as proof of receipt.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The primary use of a postage book in handling office correspondence is to
options: record the amount spent on buying stamps for outgoing mails
write down the names of all factory employees
calculate the company's daily trading profit
track the attendance of the dispatch rider
questions.explain: The **postage book** is a specialized record used to account for the value of postage stamps bought and affixed to outgoing mails, helping to control mailing expenses.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The correct standard sequence for preparing a formal outgoing letter for dispatch is
questions.explain: When preparing outgoing mail, the letter must first be **typed**, then reviewed and **signed** by an authorized person, followed by **folding** into the envelope, and finally **sealing** it before dispatch.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When an incoming letter delivered to the general office is marked "Confidential" or "Strictly Private", the mail clerk should
options: open it immediately to check for money
read it and summarize the contents for the manager
forward it unopened directly to the addressee
questions.explain: By correspondence handling rules, any mail marked "Private" or "Confidential" must not be opened by the general mail clerk; it must be **forwarded unopened** to the person it is addressed to.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Outgoing letters are usually assigned unique reference numbers (e.g., $REF/ACCT/24/01$) before they are dispatched. This is mainly to
options: prevent the letter from being stolen by armed robbers
make it easy to file a copy and trace future replies
increase the cost of postage at the post office
ensure the postman delivers it to a foreign country quickly
questions.explain: Reference numbers act as unique identifiers for letters, making it **easy to file copies and quickly trace previous correspondence** when a reply is received.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following represents a fast, modern method through which electronic correspondence comes into an organization?
questions.explain: An **E-mail** (electronic mail) is the digital way mails come into an organization over the internet, unlike P.O. Box, PMB, and dispatch riders which handle physical documents.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A major consequence of failing to maintain proper correspondence records (like the incoming and outgoing mail registers) in an office is
options: an automatic increase in employee salaries
difficulty in tracing lost letters and poor communication flow
elimination of the need for a receptionist
questions.explain: The core use of correspondence records is to document the movement of information. Without these registers, an office will experience **difficulty in tracing lost letters and a breakdown in communication flow**.
questions.subject: Business Studies
